data.title: Kusín – a massive Slavic hillfort on the Hradek hill
data.excerpt: A massive Slavic hillfort of a defensive and refuge character lies on the Hradek hill above Kusín, built above the route linking the East Slovak Lowland with the region beyond the Vihorlat. Survey and trial excavation yielded Late Bronze Age sherds, a quantity of advanced Slavic pottery and an iron suspension mount from a bucket – probably the easternmost find of its kind in the Carpathian Basin.
data.metaTitle: Kusín – a Slavic hillfort on the Hradek hill
data.metaDescription: A massive Slavic hillfort of a defensive character lies on the Hradek hill above Kusín, on the watershed of the Kusínsky and Suchý streams in eastern Slovakia.

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: The Hradek hill between the spot heights of 590 and 666 m, on the watershed of the Kusínsky and Suchý streams

keyFacts.label: Type of hillfort
keyFacts.value: A massive Slavic hillfort of a defensive and refuge character, built strategically above the route linking the East Slovak Lowland with the region beyond the Vihorlat

keyFacts.label: Dating of the occupation
keyFacts.value: Broadly from the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries to the beginning of the 11th century

keyFacts.label: Earliest finds
keyFacts.value: Stray atypical sherds of the Late Bronze Age, probably of the Gáva culture

keyFacts.label: Slavic pottery
keyFacts.value: A quantity of fragments of advanced Slavic pottery decorated with horizontal grooves and wavy lines, including a sherd with a relief mark and a fragment of a conical bowl

keyFacts.label: A rare find
keyFacts.value: An iron suspension mount from a bucket, 7.7 cm long, with no rivet holes – probably the easternmost find of its kind in the Carpathian Basin

keyFacts.label: Excavation and publication
keyFacts.value: The survey and trial excavation were written up by V. Budinský-Krička, published in the journal Nové obzory 25, Košice 1983, pp. 97–111

children.text: The Hradek hill rises on the watershed between the Kusínsky stream, which flows into the Zemplínska Šírava reservoir, and the Suchý stream, a tributary of the Kamenický stream, which flows into the Laborec, between the spot heights of 590 and 666. The very name Hradek made it possible to suppose that an archaeological site lay on the hill. We satisfied ourselves of this during a survey and a trial excavation, when we identified on it a massive Slavic hillfort, most probably of a defensive and refuge character and of strategic importance, built above an important route linking the East Slovak Lowland with the region beyond the Vihorlat.

The find material from the surface collection and the trial trenches consists of stray sherds of the Late Bronze Age and of a quantity of fragments of advanced Slavic pottery, besides which an iron catch mount from a bucket was also exceptionally found.

The Late Bronze Age sherds, mostly atypical, most probably belong to the Gáva culture. Of the more diagnostic fragments, some come from the rim parts of vessels of a shape that cannot be determined more closely, others from amphora-shaped vessels, one of which was decorated with grooves on the belly and another with a band of horizontal incised lines on the neck. The stray finds of the pottery fragments mentioned indicate that in the Late Bronze Age the hillfort was hardly occupied in any sustained way. Nevertheless, it can be admitted with a certain reserve that the beginnings of the fortification of the hill reach back as far as this period.

children.text: A more lasting Slavic occupation of the hillfort is borne out above all by the numerous finds of fragments of Slavic pottery. They are fragments of pot-shaped, mostly thin-walled vessels, made of a fine sandy clay on the wheel, brown, brownish-grey, yellowish-brown and dark grey in colour. The rim of some pots was, judging by their fragments, narrow and cut off vertically or obliquely, that of others broader and formed like a cornice, at times overhanging or even profiled, and that of yet others rounded and thickened. In the decoration discernible on the fragments, horizontal grooves clearly predominate, followed by multiple wavy lines, generally combined with bands of horizontal incised lines. Less often, simple wavy lines appear on the sherds, sometimes combined with horizontal grooves, rows of nicks, or zigzag lines made up of segments impressed with a small comb. Particularly striking is a fragment of a vessel decorated with simple wavy lines on either side of a relief rib. Fragments from the bottoms of vessels indicate pots with a base rounded on the inside. Among these fragments, special attention is undoubtedly deserved by a sherd with a relief mark consisting of a double square frame crossed by a cross, with a small circle in the middle. Finally, among the finds of Slavic pottery it is also worth drawing particular attention to a fragment of a brown conical bowl made on the wheel, because vessels of this kind are a rarity even at other Slavic settlements in eastern Slovakia.

children.text: Besides the numerous pottery fragments, a single iron object is also connected with the Slavic occupation of the hillfort at Kusín – a lateral suspension mount from a bucket, found in the occupation layer during the trial excavation on its plateau. It has the shape of an elongated triangle with a slightly offset sheet-metal plate at the junction with the loop for suspension; its end originally (
still before the object was conserved

) slightly overlapped the edge of the plate of the mount. The arched lower end of the sheet metal of the mount is bent back and forged on. The plate of the mount is 1.5 mm thick and its loop 4 mm, the mount is 7.7 cm long and its maximum width is 26.5 mm. It is worth noting in particular that it has no rivet holes.
On the basis of the finds so far, the Slavic occupation of the hillfort at Kusín (

) can be dated broadly to the period from the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries to the beginning of the 11th century. According to this, the extensive fortification of the hillfort would also fall within this span of time, bearing witness to carefully organised work by its inhabitants that was demanding from a military and strategic point of view. The find of the suspension mount from a bucket must undoubtedly also be regarded as contemporary with the Slavic pottery material from the hillfort, and we therefore date it to the wider span of time mentioned. This mount deserves particular attention above all because it is at present probably the easternmost find of its kind in the Carpathian Basin, if not in the wider central European area, but also because it draws attention to the long survival of one of the oldest forms of suspension mounts of Slavic buckets.

children.text: If we accept its preliminary dating, the construction of the massive Slavic hillfort in the Vihorlat mountains could be connected not only with the advance of the Old Hungarian tribal confederation into the Medzibodrožie region, but most probably also with the movements that followed and with the penetration of the first military retinues of the emerging Hungarian state into the south of eastern Slovakia. With its earthen defences and with the finds brought by its initial survey and excavation alone, the Slavic hillfort at Kusín appears as a further important archaeological site of its kind in eastern Slovakia.
